description: Lets the agent list, create, and update the user's own agents — their prompts, abilities, per-tool availability/permissions, and skills — and read, start, continue and monitor the user's sessions, including arming a session watch that reports when a turn settles. On by default; switch off to remove it platform-wide.

settings.label: Max Agents per User
settings.hint: How many agents this orchestrator can create for the user in total. Once the user's agent count reaches this limit, create_agent calls are refused. Prevents an orchestrator from flooding the account with hundreds of agents. Does not affect the orchestrator editing existing agents — only creation is capped.

settings.label: Allow Agent Deletion
settings.hint: Whether the agent is allowed to delete the user's agents. Off by default — agent deletion should be a deliberate human decision, not something an agent decides on its own. When off, any attempt to delete an agent is refused.

settings.label: Allow Discoverable Agents
settings.hint: Whether created agents can be marked as discoverable (visible to other users on the platform). Off by default for privacy — agent-created agents stay private to the user. When on, the agent can set discoverable=true on create_agent.

settings.label: Max Prompt Edits per Session
settings.hint: How many times the agent can edit prompts (edit_agent_prompt) in a single chat session. Catches runaway prompt-rewriting loops where the agent keeps tweaking prompts indefinitely. The counter resets when a new session starts.

settings.label: Max Agent Updates per Session
settings.hint: How many configuration changes (update_agent, set_agent_tool, set_agent_ability, manage_agent_skills) the agent can make in a single session. Catches runaway configuration loops. The counter resets when a new session starts.

settings.label: Restrict to Custom Only
settings.hint: When on, the agent can only create and edit custom agents (source='custom') — never touch templates, system agents, or app-provided agents. When off, the agent can manage any agent the user owns. Turn this on for safety when you don't want the agent modifying pre-built templates.

settings.label: Allow Session Watching
settings.hint: Whether an agent can arm a session watch (watch_sessions), which triggers it when one of your sessions settles — a turn that was running stops. When off, the tool refuses platform-wide. Note this only controls ARMING: the agent still needs the Automation ability enabled for the platform to deliver the events. Per-agent control is the normal tool permission dial — deny watch_sessions on every agent except the one you want watching.

notes.ability_changes_are_additive: set_agent_ability is ADDITIVE / independent — turning one ability on (or off) never touches any other ability the agent already has. Enabling diagnostics on an agent that already had web_access leaves web_access enabled. There is no 'enabling one disables the others' behaviour; configure each ability with its own call.
notes.bulk_set_proposal: PROPOSED (not yet built): a single 'set exactly these abilities' tool (e.g. set_agent_abilities(agent_id, abilities=[...], read_only=[...])) that diffs the agent's current enabled set against the requested set and enables/disables in one call. Today, fully re-provisioning an agent's abilities takes one set_agent_ability call per ability added AND one per ability removed, which is verbose for big reconfigurations (e.g. swapping a build agent over to a research profile). A bulk diff tool would cut a 6-ability reprovision from ~10 calls to 1 and make the desired end-state explicit. Low correctness risk because each underlying op already exists; it is purely a convenience/round-trip win. Add it as a DROP-IN tool in this ability folder (never a core edit) if prioritised.
